title: First upstream rate-limit or outage is reported as course not found

evidence.quote: if (upstreamBackoff.isRateLimited(response.status)) { ... } return c.json({ error: `Course not found: ${response.status}` }, 404);
return c.json({ error: 'Rate limited and no cached data available', retryAfter: ... }, 503);

reasoning: When CISAPI returns 429 or 503 during a live fetch, the route records a backoff failure but still returns 404. That means the first rate-limited request, even for a real course and even if stale data exists, is exposed to clients as a missing course; only later requests hit the backing-off branch that returns stale data or 503.
recommendation: Branch non-ok upstream responses by status: reserve 404 for actual not-found responses, return stale cached data when available for 429/503/5xx, and otherwise return 503/502 with retry metadata.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included course route tests cover malformed parameters and a fresh 200 response, but not non-ok browserFetch responses or stale-cache behavior during a rate limit.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock browserFetch to return 429 with an expired cached course row available and assert the response is stale 200 or 503, never 404.
minimumFixScope: Update the non-ok response handling in apps/api/src/routes/course.ts and add one route test for 429 or 503.
